subject: Night shift queueing and degraded p95/p99 for extended-context requests
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily@careml.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 23:02:15 -0800
Subject: Notice — spikes during late-night batch, 16k payloads

Hi Sean / Monica,

Quick heads-up from our ops team: starting ~22:40 PST we saw a sharp increase in API latency for several inference calls that include long histories (14k–18k tokens). The burst lasted roughly 35–40 minutes; p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s and p99 to ~6–7s for the affected routes. Error rate also ticked up (timeouts) for a subset of those requests.

We attached a small sample trace and the raw request payloads from our side (night-sample-20261129.json). This is hitting our core product flows (multi-turn summarization). Can you confirm whether this matches anything on your end? We were able to temporarily route traffic to a smaller-window model and saw immediate latency improvement.

We need:
- short explanation of root cause hypothesis
- ETA for mitigation or recommended temporary knobs we can toggle
- whether you can enable a fallback/prefix cache for these routes

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Emily

Taking this on — quick notes from the runtime side after initial triage:
- Timeline matches an autoscaling/eviction event in one of the hosted pools; during the scale activity we saw transient queueing and higher-than-expected context-restore cost for large KV caches.
- The requests in the sample are long-context (~16k tokens). Those trigger a different execution path: larger KV cache population and heavier attention-kernel memory traffic. When a worker reassigns or we evict idle workers, those in-flight requests can suffer long tail latency due to cache rehydration and blocking GPU copies.
- We pulled heap/kv stats and attached a lightweight heap snapshot. There are clear peaks in per-worker resident set that line up with the p99 spikes.

Immediate mitigations we can flip (30–90 min to push safely):
- Disable autoscale down during night window for CareML’s dedicated hosted pool (prevents eviction churn) — low risk, small extra cost.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated conversation prefixes (we can push a policy that caches the earlier tokens on the the serving edge for this tenant).
- Add a targeted canary: route CareML long-context traffic to a warmed pool with held KV caches for the next 12 hours.

Longer-term: we should prioritize an optimization to reduce rehydration latency on 12–32k windows (kernel overlap + async cache streaming). I'll open a follow-on engineering RFC.

Attachments: heap-snapshot-1129.avail (attachment stub), p95-p99-graphs-1129.png (image/png)

Emily — forwarding Marissa's findings and a couple of immediate actions we can take on our side. Proposed short action plan for CareML:

1) Enable warm pool routing for the next 12 hours (we can do this tonight). Pros: immediate p95/p99 improvement for long-context requests. Cons: small additional cost for held warm capacity.
2) If you prefer not to change routing, we can enable a soft client-side guardrail: reject requests >18k tokens with a clear HTTP 429 and guidance to truncate. We know this is disruptive to flow; this is last resort.
3) We'll keep autoscale down disabled for your tenant in the US region for the next 48 hours while we monitor.

If you approve #1 we can schedule the routing change now and confirm improved numbers within the next 30 minutes.

Also adding Sean and Aisha to any exec-level asks.

Subject: Escalation summary and exec ask — CareML nighttime tail latency

Aisha — quick summary and ask for executive visibility:

What happened: Between ~22:40–23:20 PST on 11/29 CareML observed p95/p99 regressions for extended-context inference (roughly 14k–18k tokens). Root cause (current hypothesis): transient worker eviction during autoscale combined with heavy KV cache rehydration for long-context requests, leading to queueing and blocking GPU memory operations.

Immediate actions taken:
- Marissa disabled autoscale-down for CareML's US hosted pool and spun up a warmed pool targeting long-context requests.
- Customer agreed to a warm-pool routing change; Monica scheduled the switch and will monitor.
- SRE attached heap snapshot and we flagged a follow-up engineering ticket to improve async cache streaming.

Customer impact: intermittent timeouts and elevated p99 for 35–40 minutes. CareML temporarily rerouted to a shorter-window model to keep production running; they are sensitive because this affects nightly summarization jobs.

Ask: please confirm whether we should offer a formal goodwill credit for the disruption (estimated impact window: ~40 minutes of increased tail latency; potential SLA exposure). Also need sign-off to fast-track the kernel-level fix (RFC + 2-sprint priority recommended by infra).

If we want to engage Legal/Finance for a credit, Monica can coordinate the credit amount and comms. For product prioritization, Marissa requests a small cross-functional task force (infra + serving runtime + product) to scope the low-latency rehydration work.

I'll keep this thread updated with post-change metrics.

–Sean
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
